title: Enterprise cutover dry-run simulation and QBR blueprint
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook defines a repeatable dry-run simulation for enterprise tenant cutovers and a companion synthetic QBR (Quarterly Business Review) blueprint. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions, and SRE teams running pre-cutover validations and for post-cutover QBRs that validate fidelity, costs, and operational readiness. Use this document for: planning rehearsals, validating telemetry, executing controlled cutovers, and producing a synthetic QBR package for stakeholders.

Key objectives

- Validate end-to-end telemetry, alerting, and cost-attribution for a tenant migration/cutover.
- Exercise rollback and failback procedures in a low-risk simulation.
- Produce a reproducible synthetic QBR artifact showing availability, inference economics, and quality metrics.
- Ensure cross-team coordination and clearly assigned owners for cutover day.

Primary owners and roles

- Cutover Lead: Customer Success (primary contact for the tenant) — owner: Priya Kapoor
- Technical Lead: Solutions Engineering (cutover commands and tenant config) — owner: Diego Morales
- SRE Lead: Eng-SRE (monitoring, runbook steps, capacity) — owner: Chen Wang
- Observability Owner: Eng-Platform (dashboards and traces) — owner: Alyssa Kim
- Security Gatekeeper: Security & Compliance (network and ACL approvals) — owner: Maria Jensen

Preconditions and environment

- Target tenant in staging with production-like data subset.
- Telemetry forwarding enabled (metrics -> MetricsCluster.prod, traces -> TracingCluster.redwood).
- Access: all owners have temporary escalation access in the access control system.
- Canary model version pinned to v2.3.1-quant (or the version planned for production).

SLOs and pass/fail thresholds for the dry-run

| Metric | Pass threshold (staging) | Warning threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| P50 latency (inference) | < 60ms | 60–120ms | Measured token-start to token-end for typical 64-token request |
| P95 latency (inference) | < 160ms | 160–300ms | If above warning, reduce batching or increase pool size |
| Error rate (5m window) | < 0.1% | 0.1%–0.5% | Includes 5xx and model-internal decode failures |
| Availability (5m) | >= 99.9% | 99.5%–99.9% | Successful streaming connection and final token received |
| Token cost delta (baseline) | <= +10% | +10%–+25% | Compare to baseline tenant cost for identical synthetic workload |
| KV cache hit ratio | >= 70% | 50%–70% | Important for chat-style workloads |

Pre-run checklist (minimum)

1. Confirm schedule with tenant stakeholders and all owners (48h notice).
2. Provision staging capacity that mirrors target production config (GPU type, batch size, pool size).
3. Export and pin synthetic prompt set (see "Synthetic test plan") and upload to the Eval Harness under ID: cutover-dryrun-<tenant>-2026-01.
4. Verify telemetry pipelines: sample metrics present in dashboards within 2 minutes of synthetic traffic start.
5. Validate ACLs and network paths for private tenants (VPN, peering, firewall rules).
6. Prepare rollback script and acceptance criteria (stored in tenant playbook repo).

Synthetic test plan (what to run)

- Duration: 45m baseline -> 15m scale-up -> 30m soak -> 10m failover test -> 15m rollback validation.
- Traffic mix: 60% chat-completion (avg 120 tokens), 30% embeddings (batch=16), 10% rerank.
- Burst profile: simulate 3x traffic for 2 minutes at minute 30 to validate autoscaling and queueing.
- Data masks: replace all PII in prompts; use pseudonymization preset.

Example synthetic runner command

curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/simulate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${SIM_KEY}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"suite_id":"cutover-dryrun-tenant42","duration_min":105,"mix":{"chat":0.6,"embeddings":0.3,"rerank":0.1}}'

Monitoring and alerts to validate live

- Dashboards: Tenant Overview, Model Pool Health, Token Economics, Streaming Errors.
- Critical alerts (must be ON): high-error-rate (5m > 0.5%), p95-latency-breach (5m > 300ms), queue-length (> 500 requests), billing-anomaly (> +20% compared to baseline).
- Tracing: sample 1% of requests with full flamegraph recording for the 15m scale-up window.

Dry-run timeline and responsibilities (example runbook)

1) T-60m: Preflight check (Cutover Lead)
   - Confirm all stakeholders present on the run channel (#cs-cutover-tenant42-run).
   - SRE verifies pool capacity and autoscaler status.
2) T-30m: Baseline traffic start (Synthetic runner)
   - Observe baseline metrics; collect initial QBR snapshot.
3) T-15m: Scale-up simulation
   - Trigger 3x burst for 2 minutes. Solutions verifies request routing and fallback paths.
4) T+0m: Soak window (15–30m)
   - Monitor KV cache hit ratio, model decoding errors, and memory usage.
5) T+30m: Failover exercise
   - Simulate primary region degradation: route 50% of requests to fallback region; validate graceful degradation (no more than 2x latency increase).
6) T+45m: Rollback and data integrity check
   - Execute rollback script: revert routing to original variant and validate session continuity for 95% of synthetic sessions.
7) T+60m: Post-run debrief and artifact snapshot
   - Capture dashboards, traces, alert logs, and cost estimate.

Rollback and emergency procedures

- If error-rate > 1% sustained for 5m: abort scale-up and roll back model variant to previous stable version (v2.3.0). Owner: Solutions Engineering.
- If availability < 99% for 10m: escalate to SRE on-call and initiate tenant short-circuit to a safety pool (see runbook ID: safepool-switch-2025).
- If billing spike exceeds +40% within 1h: pause synthetic runner and open finance notification.

Post-run deliverables (artifact checklist)

- Synthetic QBR PDF (auto-generated): includes availability graphs, latency percentiles, cost delta, and quality regressions (NLG BLEU/ROUGE-like scores where applicable).
- Runbook incident log: timeline with commands executed and owner notes.
- Telemetry package: zipped Grafana dashboard JSON, 5m sampled traces, metric export (Prometheus textfile).
- Action items: prioritized list and owner assignment.

Synthetic QBR blueprint (sections to include)

1. Executive summary (1 page): high-level status, go/no-go recommendation, top risks.
2. Availability and latency (2 pages): p50/p95/p99 + short narrative on tail behaviour.
3. Inference economics (1–2 pages): token cost vs baseline, caching effect, suggestions for batching/quantization.
4. Quality and regression checks (1 page): sample prompts, reference outputs, regression flagging rules.
5. Operational readiness (1 page): runbook gaps, alert tuning, and capacity recommendations.
6. Action plan and owners (1 page): 30/60/90 day remediation items.

Template metrics to include in the QBR (minimum)

- Uptime (7d window)
- P50/P95/P99 latency (end-to-end)
- Error rate (5m and 60m windows)
- Token consumption and cost delta vs baseline (7d)
- KV cache hit ratio (soak window)
- Number of rollbacks / failovers during run
- Top 5 error signatures and sample traces

Common failure modes discovered in past dry-runs

- Misconfigured telemetry forwarding (missing tag: tenant_id) -> dashboards show no per-tenant split. Fix: validate metric labels before run.
- Autoscaler cooldown too long -> inability to scale during bursts. Fix: lower cooldown to 30s for cutover pool.
- Private-network ACL missing outbound to MetricsCluster -> missing metrics. Fix: preflight network test.

Appendices

A. Command snippets

- Rollback model variant (CLI):
  redwoodctl tenant update --tenant tenant42 --model v2.3.0 --force

- Switch to safepool (SRE):
  redwoodctl pool route --tenant tenant42 --target safepool-standby --reason "dry-run failover"

B. Dashboards to snapshot (IDs)
- tenant-overview-42, model-pool-health, token-econ-tenant42, streaming-errors-42
